thread:
olivia: FYI — synth notes from this morning's roadmap sync. Need alignment on regional failover guardrails, customer-impact gating, and launch criteria for the topology changes.
kevin: can we list explicit gating criteria? I'm thinking latency SLOs, data residency commitments, and multi-tenant isolation tiers.
ajay: +1. Tentative gating: p99 < 400ms under 75th percentile regional load, canary pass in at least 1 adjacent region, and automated fallback to a compatible model variant on capacity pressure.
maria: Customer ask: LargeCommerce needs strict isolation plus transparent failover behavior and a schedule for rolling upgrade windows. They also want a runbook for cold-start scenarios.
ryan: We should quantify cost impact. Cross-region routing and cache warming will add egress and warm-pool costs — need a per-customer uplift estimate.
olivia: Draft policy notes: 1) Default regional affinity (session stickiness) for latency-critical tenants; 2) Cross-region failover only for SLA-backed customers or opt-in; 3) Soft-quarantine for unknown/new tenants during automated failovers; 4) Fallback to quantized/cheaper model family when latency or capacity thresholds hit.
kevin: How do we keep KV cache warm during failover? Full replication is expensive. We need a minimal approach.
ajay: Proposal: lightweight prefix metadata replication + async top-K session prefetch. Not full KV replication but enough to avoid p99 spikes for hot sessions. I'll sketch sequence diagram.
olivia: Ops note — any prefetch/replication plan affects storage and network quotas; SRE sign-off required before canary.
infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: routing-topology-prototype -> staging on 2024-07-12T03:00:00Z (ID: deploy-7891)
maria: Launch checklist draft:
- SLO validation with synthetic cross-region traffic
- Cost projection with billing sim <= 25% uplift for reserved customers
- Canary plan + automated rollback scripts
- Customer-facing runbook and opt-in window
- Security review for cross-region data handling
kevin: Add: integration tests for tenant-scoped KV cache behavior and failure injection scenarios.
ryan: Add: billing simulation for egress, model swaps, and warm-pool deltas.
olivia: Next steps: ajay to spec cache-warming approach and failure modes, kevin to author test matrix and integrate failure injections, maria to draft customer comms + runbook. Sync tomorrow 10am PT.
ajay: I'll open a spec PR today with diagrams and the tradeoffs table (latency vs replication cost).
kevin: I'll pair with eng-sre on the test infra and schedule fault-injection runs.
maria: I'll prepare the initial customer comms + FAQ focused on data residency, cost optics, and opt-out path.
olivia: If no major objections by EOD we'll lock this as the working proposal and move the prototype to staging :thumbsup:
